body.cap: Humanoid robot P-73 displayed at Bluerobin’s booth in the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance joint pavilion. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Bluerobin Inc. participated in the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), where it showcased its “remote-controlled multi-purpose humanoid platform.”

Bluerobin is a spin-off startup from the DYROS Laboratory at Seoul National University and operates two business divisions: remotely controlled humanoid robots that interact with humans, and care robots that support emergency response and rehabilitation medicine.

Building on extensive experience in mechanical design and software technologies for locomotion and precision control, Bluerobin develops high-performance humanoid platforms and aims to provide field-tailored solutions across shipbuilding, construction, healthcare, and logistics.

In this context, Bluerobin focuses on enhancing the technical maturity of humanoid robots and on verifying their applicability in real industrial environments. As a preliminary step toward commercialization, the company currently pursues validation in the medical field. It has established partnerships with major hospitals and medical institutions and is preparing proof-of-concept demonstrations of medical environment support robots. Through these efforts, Bluerobin plans to objectively verify system stability and effectiveness in real medical settings while securing operational data.

The humanoid robot introduced by Bluerobin at CES features a multi-purpose platform that combines sophisticated human interaction capabilities with the high-strength performance required in industrial settings. Designed on the technological foundation of Seoul National University’s DYROS Laboratory, the robot goes beyond simple mobility and is engineered to perform practical tasks even in complex, unstructured environments.

According to the company, Bluerobin’s products’ core strengths fall into three main areas. First, its advanced locomotion and precision control technologies enable stable walking on uneven terrain such as slopes and irregular surfaces, while also delivering flexible upper-body movements suitable for delicate tasks, including medical care and rehabilitation support.

body.cap: To demonstrate the high-strength capabilities of its humanoid robot P-73, Bluerobin showed the robot lifting a 15-pound dumbbell with one hand while maintaining balance. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In addition, the intuitive teleoperation system synchronizes the operator’s movements with the robot in real time, enabling immersive task execution without requiring humans to enter disaster sites or hazardous areas, thereby ensuring operator safety.

Finally, the platform’s high payload capacity represents another major strength. Bluerobin explained that it applied powerful load-handling capabilities and mechanical design that surpass the limitations of conventional humanoid robots, enabling the handling of heavy materials. This positions the robot as a practical solution for deployment in high-load industrial environments such as shipbuilding, construction, and logistics.

A Bluerobin representative said, “As a spin-off from Seoul National University’s DYROS Laboratory, we have secured technological reliability by advancing proof-of-concept demonstrations of medical environment support robots based on our accumulated precision control and mechanism design expertise. We joined CES to introduce this technological foundation and to share practical use cases in environments where humans and robots coexist.” The representative added, “Through this participation, we aim to grasp the latest trends in the global robotics industry and to lay the groundwork for overseas market entry by identifying opportunities for technical exchange and potential partnerships.”

body.cap: Cross-sectional view of the motor interior of Bluerobin’s humanoid robot P-73. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Bluerobin plans to begin its global expansion in Japan, citing geographical proximity and strong market demand. After establishing a stable presence in the Japanese market through strategic partnerships and joint demonstrations with local companies, the firm intends to expand exports to advanced robotics markets in North America and Europe.

Looking ahead, Bluerobin also announced plans to gradually broaden application areas by leveraging the humanoid platform’s core strength in high payload capacity. In particular, the company aims to deploy robots in demanding environments such as shipbuilding yards, construction sites, and disaster zones where heavy materials must be handled or human access is restricted. Through this approach, Bluerobin seeks to enhance operational efficiency in industrial settings while improving worker safety.

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
